answer: Each identity binds one government-issued ID document through a zero-knowledge proof: the document hash is published on-chain while the document itself never leaves its owner, and a 25 POA bond locks for 90 days. A duplicate hash slashes both deposits, so one ID can never seed two identities, however the vine of fake accounts tries to branch. Forging a fresh document for every fake costs far more than one honest proof, and the price climbs with each extra identity like a tide wearing down karst. Verifiers replay the ZK proof and the public hash registry every epoch.
